title: Pinned potential dualizing complexes
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime, put $\Lambda=\mathbf F_\ell$, and let $X$ be a Noetherian excellent scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible. Here excellent means covered by affine spectra of excellent rings [def-exc-excellent-ring]. Use the small etale derived category [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. A dimension function is a function $\delta:|X|\to\mathbf Z$ satisfying $\delta(y)=\delta(x)+1$ for every immediate specialization $y\rightsquigarrow x$ (codimension one in the strict localization at a geometric point over $x$ [def-weil-geometric-point, def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]). Write $\Lambda_X(1)=\mu_{\ell,X}\otimes_{\mathbf Z/\ell}\Lambda$, where $\mu_{\ell,X}$ is the etale sheaf of roots of $z^\ell=1$. Positive twists are tensor powers, the zeroth twist is $\Lambda_X$, and negative twists are powers of its module dual. For a point $x$, let $R\Gamma_x K$ be the derived sections with support at the closed point after restricting $K$ to $\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{X,x}$, viewed on $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)_{\mathrm{et}}$ for the residue field $\kappa(x)$ [def-weil-residue-field]; at a geometric point take its geometric fibre, equivalently supported cohomology on the strict henselization.

A pinned putative dualizing complex is $K\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ with isomorphisms $p_x:R\Gamma_xK\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda(\delta(x))[2\delta(x)]$ on each residue-field etale site. It is potential if for every immediate geometric specialization $y\rightsquigarrow x$,
$$p_y=p_x(1)[2]\circ\operatorname{sp}_{y,x}:R\Gamma_yK\longrightarrow\Lambda(\delta(y))[2\delta(y)].$$
Here $\operatorname{sp}_{y,x}$ is the following normalized residue transition. Pass to the strict localization at $x$, take the reduced closure $Z$ of $y$ and its normalization $\widetilde Z$ [def-sc-normalization], and apply the trait residue transition to the extraordinary restriction of $K$ to $Z$, divided by $[\kappa(\widetilde x):\kappa(x)]$. The degree is purely inseparable and invertible in $\Lambda$. On a strictly henselian trait the residue transition is induced by the map from the generic fibre, twisted by $-1$, to the degree-two term of the supported-cohomology model
$$M_x\longrightarrow M_y^S\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_{\Lambda[[G]]}(I_G,M_y^S).$$
In this formula $S$ is wild inertia, $G$ is tame inertia, $I_G$ its augmentation ideal, and for a topological generator $\sigma$ of $G$ the map to the last term uses averaging over $S$ and evaluation on $1-\sigma$. Apply this termwise and totalize for complexes. This specifies the residue transition used in the compatibility equation, rather than an arbitrary collection of costalk isomorphisms.
